selected_patterns.why: The configfs lifetime is intrusive and callback-owned; the subsystem/group/item model must stay pinned and drive state transitions explicitly.
tag_set, request_queue, gendisk, and load/unload teardown must be modeled as acquire/register/drop pairs rather than ad-hoc raw pointer flows.

selected_patterns.placement: rust/kernel/block/mq/request.rs and hctx support added under rust/kernel/block/mq
selected_patterns.why: queue_rq/complete/timeout/poll all run through blk-mq callbacks and require explicit ownership transfer rules. The driver must not hold a wide mutable borrow over queue-owned state.

selected_patterns.pattern: pinned timer object with narrow callback surface
selected_patterns.why: Timer callbacks outlive the submission stack and need a safe pinned wrapper that exposes restart/cancel/forward semantics without leaking raw hrtimer usage into the driver.

selected_patterns.pattern: Rust-native owned storage with safe page-copy boundary
selected_patterns.placement: rnull runtime internals, not C radix-tree clones
selected_patterns.why: The C radix-tree/page-cache implementation is an engineering choice, not the semantic target. A Rust-owned storage model preserves behavior while keeping unsafe concentrated below the driver layer.

abstraction_sources_in_priority_order.source: mature public abstractions reasonably forward-portable from current tree
new minimal abstractions added in rust/kernel/*
applied_to: safe request metadata and segment walking

abstraction_sources_in_priority_order.source: minimal generic helpers only where Rust cannot call a needed inline/macro path directly

explicit_non_selections.pattern: driver directly using bindings::* for blk-mq/configfs/time
explicit_non_selections.reason: Violates the zero-unsafe driver requirement and defeats the audit trail.
Too permissive for request completion ownership and callback interleavings.

explicit_non_selections.pattern: lifting official rnull private structure layout verbatim before stage 9

why_not_thinner: Without the queue/hctx/timer/request abstractions in rust/kernel, the driver would have to manipulate raw request pointers, blk_mq_hw_ctx driver_data, and hrtimer callbacks directly, which would either reintroduce unsafe into the driver or force helper creep.
